# Knives of Khaine

*Pages PDF 112-118*

## **Knives of Khaine**
## **The Blood-Drenched Devoted**
Murder is commonplace in Druchii society, and _Temple of Spite_ is no exception. For some elves, taking lives is more than a means to an end, it is the ultimate sacrament. All dark elves venerate Khaine as chief amongst the Cytharai, yet the true faithful stand apart from the rest of dark elven society. The Knives of Khaine are those inhabitants of _Temple of Spite_ who share their god’s earnest love of killing, and hope for no further reward than the chance to take another life. Anointed by Death Hag Kheitalla, they seek greater glory in the palm of Khaine’s bloody hand. 

The Knives of Khaine are the favoured congregation who gather at the temple dominating Valeth’s Palace. Their number include the cult’s witch elves, temple attendants, and any cultists who impress the death hag with their devotion to the BloodyHanded God, ranging from esteemed corsairs to raving lowborn madmen. The Knives are among the most feared Druchii on board the ark, they act in the name of Khaine and so claim to represent his mortal vessel, Malerion. This causes friction with other factions, as their zeal is annoying at best and fatal at worst. 

**Dominate the Ark.** They are too cunning to make their ambitions known, but the Knives of Khaine wish to seize the ark’s power structures and turn decisions by the Black Convocation their way. Kheitalla is among _Temple of Spite’s_ highest authorities, who covets further power and use it to inflict holy violence. 

## **On the Black Ark**
The Knives worship in Khaine’s temple, which stands at the aft of the ark. They join ceremonies, witness sacrifices, and attend for personal worship. Khaine’s devout followers live throughout the ark, amongst their fellow inhabitants, while the witch elves and cult hierarchy dwell in cloistered cells within the temple bounds. 

The temple of Khaine has privilege on the ark and a seat on the Black Convocation. It is entitled to one tenth of captives as a sacrificial tithe. If the Knives of Khaine suspect Khaine is deprived of his due, they feel honour-bound to seek recompense. 

## **Goals**
**Sacrifice to Khaine.** The Knives of Khaine must sacrifice to their god. Captives are the main source of blood, though if they cannot obtain a steady supply the Khainites resort to condemned dark elves, those out of favour with the Black Convocation, or lowborn Druchii. Sacrifice is a ritual act of devotion to fill the temple’s cauldron of blood. This is a powerful religious symbol, and should the blood run low, the Knives of Khaine believe their god will forsake them. 

**Proselytise.** As religious fanatics, the Knives of Khaine see it as their duty to inspire others to greater reverence. This can extend to non-elves, for Khaine appreciates all acts of murder in his name, no matter who holds the knife. 

**Slay victims.** Khaine expects his followers to shed blood and bring the fury of the elves to every waking moment. The Knives of Khaine believe they must kill to earn their god’s favour and only survival forces them to restrain their urges. 

A closed community surrounded by ocean cannot easily accommodate perpetual violence. Members of the Black Convocation try to persuade Death Hag Kheitalla to restrain her followers, not through concern for their suffering or a lack of piety, but to preserve a functioning society on the ark. The Khainites, especially witch elves, believe their god gives them a unique role, and they enjoy flouting convention through violent provocations calculated to create problems resolvable only through more murder. 

## **Death Night on the Ark**
Perhaps the greatest threat to the ark’s society is Death night. Kheitalla insists on her witch elves’ god-given right to kill anyone on Death night, no matter the consequences. helbane is reluctant to risk losing more elves from the reduced population. an awkward arrangement prevails in which the crew see to it that captives are released on Death night for the witch elves to hunt. if Characters are chosen, they could escape captivity if they evade the prowling Khainites. The Knives resent this arrangement, and Kheitalla privately tells her followers to murder as they wish on Khaine’s sacred night. 

## **Rivals and Allies**
The Temple’s tithe of one in ten captives causes resentment and fear. During long voyages or in times of crisis, the Death Hag demands even more lives, which kills more dark elves than any other cause. Kheitalla’s bloody-minded religiosity and permissive attitude towards her followers sets back Helbane’s ambitions and cannot be easily solved by eliminating her, as the other Khainites are no less zealous. If the fleetmaster moved against the cult, he would face serious political ramifications and assassination attempts back in Naggaroth. 

Kheitalla and her acolytes have an instinctive distrust of magic and, while they officially respect Morathi as the mother and close adviser of the Dread King, they conspire against the ark’s sorceresses. The Knives of Khaine are also vehemently opposed to followers of Slaanesh, and there are rumours that members of the coven are involved in a cult to the Dark Prince. 

Because her rites are compromised by long journeys at sea with dwindling sacrifices, Kheitalla demands constant raids for captives. The ark’s reaver captains agree on few things, but all hate the hag’s zealous captive-taking — it steals from their spoils, detracts from their own ambitions, and none relish taking orders from any but the fleetmaster. 

## **Internal Tensions**
The Knives of Khaine are perhaps the most unified faction on the _Temple of Spite_ , though they are still dark elves with their inherent rivalries. 

The witch elves compete at murder, hoping to show Khaine their devotion through creative, copious death-dealing. Sabotaging one another is frowned upon, so ritual combat is the preferred means to hinder rivals. 

The Disciple of Khaine, Hulreth, presents the Knives of Khaine with a dilemma. Even the most zealous recognise that his indiscriminate murders risk uniting other factions against the cultists as targets for revenge attacks, and he also enjoys killing fellow Khainites. There is a growing sense among the Knives that the ironic sacrifice of Hulreth might please their god. The assassin Dagulus intends to try his hand, if he can ensure sufficient support from the witch elves should he succeed. 

There is tension between Death Hag Kheitalla and the Hag Haidrath. The hag is a Bride of Burning Blood, a subcult of witch elves who believe Khaine values only blood shed during the heat of battle. Given the death hag’s appetite for sacrificing captives, the two have theological differences which may boil over into direct conflict. 

## **In the Old World**
When the Knives of Khaine land in the Old World, they are there to kill and take captives for sacrifice. Unlike many fellow dark elves, pragmatism rarely overcomes religious zeal or the frenzy that takes hold of witch elves in combat. 

And yet they do have a streak of cunning. There is an undercurrent of reverence for the Bloody-handed God in every elf culture, and the Knives of Khaine balance the psychology of awe and terror with killing, especially where Eonir or Asrai are the victims. When the Witch Elves slaughter their Old World kin, they leave survivors, hoping to stoke bloodlust and tempt them closer to Khaine, just as their forbears were seduced during the Sundering. 

## **Meeting the Khainites**
An encounter with the Knives of Khaine usually begins and ends with combat: a religion founded on bloody murder does not inspire conversation or negotiation. Characters should expect to fight for their lives; the most fortunate will die in combat rather than end their days eviscerated on the altar of Khaine. 

In some circumstances, the Khainites suppress their murderous desires to bargain with Characters. Khaine respects guile in service of bloodshed, and most killers can hide their nature before choosing the best moment to strike. Should the party meet an individual Khainite who cannot beat them in a fight, they seek advantage through honeyed words or subterfuge, hoping to slip away to find reinforcements. 

The Knives of Khaine consider themselves above politics, but they are not stupid. If the party work for a powerful patron on the ark, it may be expedient to spare them. Some witch elves like to toy with their victims, and enjoy watching lesser species indulge in killing themselves, so they may goad the party to attack another enemy, potentially even helping. 

- **Dagulus** , **Varien** , and **Zelekendel** are Khainite Assassins. Varien works undercover as one of Helbane’s minstrels. Zelekendel is assigned to kill on behalf of the Reaver Council, though he ultimately takes orders from Death Hag Kheitalla. 

- 8 Acolytes keep the temple (Dark Elf Servants). 

## **Find the Lady**
exploring the Depths, the party stumble across a bedraggled, gaunt elf. Lady Seraphiel was marked for sacrifice in the temple of Khaine, but she escaped by disguising herself as an acolyte of Khaine. Now a fugitive, she is terrified the Knives are getting closer to her hiding place. she begs the Characters to keep her location secret and offers a substantial reward if they help her return to Marienburg. soon the party meet hag Dralthari and several witch elves who claim they can _smell_ seraphiel on them. if the Characters reveal her location, the cult may even be willing to spare their lives. 

## **Anointed for Greatness**
Witch elves descend on a village in a frenzy of blood, screaming as they dismember any who come close. When haidruil raises her dagger to strike a Character, she halts, eyes widening. she sees a crimson shimmer coiling across the Character’s skin — the Mark of Khaine, visible to his most faithful. haidruil hisses to her sisters to stand down, declaring the Character sacred. They must be dragged before Kheitalla. 

## **Disposition**
The Knives of Khaine include the ark’s temple hierarchy and a cohort of devoted Khainites. 

- **Death Hag Kheitalla** commands the cult on _Temple of Spite._ Her attendants are six permanently-terrified cult servants (Dark Elf Servants). 

- **Hags Haidreth** and **Nyxira** each lead 15 Brides of Khaine, the Witch Elves who serve the temple. 

- **Hulreth** is a Disciple of Khaine, and resident in the temple. 

- A cadre of 5 Executioners (Dark Elf Elites) guard the temple as emissaries of Har Ganeth and Hag Queen Hellebron. **Draich Master Asperon** and the four Executioners loathe life at sea. 

- 64 devoted cultists live throughout the ark, including Corsairs, Beastmasters, lowborn, and soldiers from the warhost. If Kheitalla calls on them in Khaine’s name, they obey her over the fleetmaster. 

## **Appearance**
Witch elves take the field with minimal armour, protecting themselves with their faith, robes, and blood. Temple servants and other cultists wear garb typical of their calling. When fighting for the temple, they don red hoods and adorn themselves with grisly trophies taken in battle. 

Witch elves scream during combat or chant _‘Khaela Furdiekh Mensha Farmiekh Khaine’_ , a repetitive incantation to their god. 

## **The Quarry — Easy Encounter**
An injured captive flees desperately from a witch elf pursuer, scrambling past the Characters. Esteban bleeds profusely from numerous cuts (1 _Bleeding_ Condition) which slows him down. The chase proceeds at a lackadaisical pace: his pursuer can be heard singing from some distance away. If the Characters choose to help, they must support Esteban and slow or stop the bleeding. The trail of blood makes it easy to track his path. 

If the Characters are caught with Esteban, the witch elf pursuer, Maelira, is amused and invites them to aid in the sacrifice. This offer is made only once, and should the characters betray Esteban, they earn favour with the cult. Otherwise, Madeira fights for her prize, calling for aid if outnumbered. 

If Esteban survives, he can describe the disposition of the Cult of Khaine on board, learned while he was in their captivity. Maelira is also happy to educate the characters on the nature of Khaine, and if she is sated by Esteban’s death, she espouses her god’s virtues. 

- **Maelira** is a Dark Elf Lowborn (City) Witch Elf with the _Champion_ Trait. 

- **Esteban** is a human captive. 

## **The Wrong Elves — Medium Encounter**
A band of Khainites believe they have discovered a secret meeting of Slaanesh worshippers and they seek to kill them all. The party witness a battle erupt from a doorway below the Fleetmaster’s Bastion as Hag Haidreth, her witch elves, and a handful of acolytes fight with masked dark elves. The Khainites are winning, as masked Druchii scatter in every direction. Passersby also make a run for it, knowing the screams and laughter of witch elves never means anything good. 

The hectic violence spirals past the Characters, as injured Druchii search for hiding places and Khainites try to cut them down. They can hide, flee, or join the battle. The masked dark elves are conspirators plotting the downfall of Lord Tualarc. They are not Slaaneshi cultists, but they do want to keep their identity secret and survive. The Characters could help conceal one from the Khainites or fight at their side. If they kill the conspirator, then a pursuing witch elf offers an ironic thanks before attacking them in turn. 

- Hag Haidreth fights with three Witch Elves. 

- Five Knives of Khaine (An Executioner, one Highborn Entourage, a Corsair, and two Servants). 

- The conspirators are 12 Druchii Warriors and one Druchii Officer. 

## **An Orgy of Blood — Hard Encounter**
Kheitalla stands atop the Caudron of Blood, screaming imprecations to Khaine as she leads the Knives in a religious ceremony. The air is thick with incense and coppery vapours. Around the Cauldron, robed witch elves chant in perfect unison. Their pale faces are daubed with ash and crimson sigils, while their hands are slick with sacrificial blood. 

Eight victims lie bound on stone slabs set in a ring around the shrine, their throats marked with ritual cuts, and blood already seeping into the grooves carved beneath them. One by one, the Khainite cultists step forward to slice a throat and so offer up a life to their god. After each sacrifice, the Cauldron bubbles more violently, steaming with scarlet mist and spitting drops of boiling gore onto the stones. 

The congregation of Khainites are armed with poisoned daggers and daubed with blood. This ritual brings them closer to Khaine and none will tolerate interference — either to free the sacrifices or otherwise disrupt their worship. 

The final sacrifice is an important ally or patron for the party. It could be someone who protects them, a Druchii patron, someone with information they want, or a dark elf whose favour they need. 

Freeing the last sacrifice is possible with ingenuity, taking advantage of the Khainites’ religious delirium, or even offering an alternative victim. 

If all eight victims die, the Cauldron boils over and the air thickens. The worshippers chant louder and louder as they enter a religious frenzy, tearing at themselves and others to release more blood. If the Characters are caught in this, they must fend off _Frenzied_ cultists. The Khainites do not distinguish between friend and enemy, so escape is difficult if not impossible. 

The congregation consists of: 

- Death Hag Kheitalla. 

- Hags Haidreth and Nyxira. 

- 16 Witch Elves armed only with poisoned daggers (black lotus) and no armour. 

- 4 Executioners (Dark Elf Elites). 

- 16 Knives of Khaine armed only with poisoned daggers (black lotus) and no armour (6 Dark Elf Druchii Warriors, 3 Dark Elf Scouts, 5 Dark Elf Servants, and 2 Dark Elf Corsairs). 

## **Selthira Heartrender**
Just as Khaine has a thousand faces, Selthira seeks to honour him by murdering in a thousand different ways. She accomplished her goal many years ago, but each time she draws closer to a thousand, she discounts more deaths for being too similar in method to one she committed before. Selthira has a smug sense of superiority, believing her creative approach to worship brings Khaine’s favour, making her greater in his eyes than her fellow witch elves. 

Hag Haidreth believes Selthira is ambitious and self-absorbed, putting herself ahead of her superiors in the cult. The witch elf cares little what the hag or even the death hag think, she seeks only Khaine’s favour and her own elevation. 

Selthira has the archetypal look of a witch elf, pale flesh, barbed armour plates, and a silvered headdress which holds her long hair away from her face. She carries several different weapons, tools for delivering ever-more creative deaths. Selthira stares with unusual intensity at all she meets, mulling over new ways to end their life. In combat, she screams with undue pleasure, though her speaking voice is slow and silken. 

Unbeknownst to Selthira, she has attracted the attention of the Dark Prince. Slaanesh has slipped into a corner of her mind, attracted by Selthira’s perfectionism and pride.

## **Traits and Talents**
**Battle Rage:** If eligible, enter the _Frenzy_ state at will, without having to Test. When leaving _Frenzy_ state, lose Advantage to lose a _Fatigued_ Condition. 

**Combat Reflexes:** Combat Initiative counts as 70. 

**Dual Wielder:** When fighting with two weapons the character does not have to lose Advantage to make a free attack with their second weapon. 

**Etiquette (Cult of Khaine):** The characters can blend in socially with the chosen groups, so long as they are dressed and acting appropriately. 

**Frenzy:** See _Frenzy_ in the **WFRP Core Rulebook** . 

**Hatred (High Elves):** See _Hatred_ in the **WFRP Core Rulebook** . 

**Night Vision:** See clearly for 20 yards and extend the illumination distance of light sources by 20 yards. 

**Read/Write:** Can read and write. 

**Strike to Injure:** When rolling on a Critical Wound table, roll twice and choose the preferred result. Further, ignore the Called Shot penalty when going for a silent takedown. 

## **Trappings**
Blood-stained Robes, Four Sacred Daggers, Two Swords, Vial of Black Lotus Blade Venom, Vial of Zha’Kheril (see page 59) 

## **Hag Haidrath**
Haidrath is a wild thing, ill-suited to life on _Temple of Spite_ . One of the younger hags in the Cult of Khaine, she ascended to her position as one of the Brides of Burning Blood, witch elves who believe Khaine values only victims killed in battle. She has no interest in sacrificing captives, so life on the ark offers few outlets for her form of worship. As such, she stalks the ark seeking opponents to duel and kill, carving Khaine’s rune on their chest just before they die, which sends their soul to him rather than their own death god. 

The witch elves under Haidreth’s leadership respect her savagery in combat, while other Khainites find her practices eccentric. She has the distant, wandering stare of a predator and a wild mane of hair, matted with blood and bound with thorny briars. Her clothing and skin are blood-spattered and she hangs grisly trophies about her person. Haidreth speaks with a low growl. 

Haidreth has a small following amongst the ark’s beastmasters, who admire her predatory nature. They occasionally release captives for her to pursue and fight as sacrifices for Khaine. In return, Haidreth respects Khaine’s sister Anath Raema, and occasionally visits the goddess’ shrine in the Stalkers’ Spire.

## **Hulreth, Disciple of Khaine**
Perhaps the most fulfilled elf aboard _Temple of Spite_ , Hulreth is a theologian, philosopher, and enthusiastic murderer. He is affable and enjoys discussing his ideas, especially with victims. He holds that while murder is the finest form of art, it is also a basic need he must indulge, as simple as hunger or thirst. 

Hulreth is a Disciple of Khaine, a rare subcult originating in Clar Karond. Disciples revere Khaine in his aspect as Deathbringer, the merciless slayer, perfecting the art of torture and murder as a dispassionate tribute to their god. Hulreth enjoys many privileges usually reserved for witch elves, and is permitted to conduct certain rites using a cauldron blood, for which he wears an iron mask in emulation of Khaine’s first priests. His status also protects him from the consequences of wanton murder across the ark.
